## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
The smallest measured N (4000) already exceeds the L1d spill point (N≈949), so the L1d→L2 transition is not directly observable. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 10.009 ns/p at N=4000 to 7.907 at N=262000 — classic overhead amortization at small N. Crossing the L2 spill (N≈60787) produces no knee: N=16000 gives 8.226 and N=65000 gives 8.078, a gentle continued decline. Beyond N=262000 the curve is FLAT at ~8.05–8.06 ns/p through N=4M. Raising the death rate lifts the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.05 the large-N floor sits at ~8.3–8.9, and at q=0.25 it rises to ~10.2. The N-shape is invariant across death rates — death raises the floor, not the slope.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 8.73 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01, which is 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never approaches the ceiling at any N or death rate. At q=0.01 the large-N bandwidth is stable at 8.5–8.7 GB/s; at q=0.05 it regresses to 7.7–8.3; at q=0.25 it collapses to ~6.75 GB/s. The transition is driven by death rate, not by N — the branchy respawn path (37 `bl` calls to `spawn`) dominates cost as churn rises, pulling bandwidth down by 23% between q=0.01 and q=0.25.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle math. The compute loop (0x100055460–0x100055680) operates entirely on scalar single-precision registers: `ldp s5, s6`, `ldr s17`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fsub s5`, `fcvtzs`, `fcmp`, `csel`. The histogram reports zero vector-suffixed instructions. The only SIMD usage appears in the mask-scan path (`ldp q1, q0`, `orr.16b v0, v1, v0`, `ext.16b`) — a bulk byte-check for non-zero mask entries, not per-particle vectorization. The scatter writes are byte-granular: `strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]` for three sequential RGB bytes, plus `strb w11, [x23, x0]` for the mask. This scalar compute plus byte-granular scatter explains why bandwidth stalls at 35% of ceiling — the code cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler emitted no auto-vectorization of the per-particle computation (zero vector-suffixed instructions, all scalar `s`-register math), and achieved bandwidth never exceeds 8.73 GB/s = 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The byte-granular scatter stores (`strb` ×3 per particle) and 37 branchy `spawn` calls cap performance regardless of death rate, so the hypothesis fails even at q=0.01.
